Thanks for sending the MSA skeleton. We did a first pass and attached our redline (redline_MSA_20260301.docx) and a marked-up Order Form. Two items cropped up that are blockers for our GC team:

1) The damages exclusion — your proposed clause excludes consequential/special/incidental/punitive damages but includes a catch-all tied to "foreseeability." Our counsel insists on replacing that with a proximate-cause standard to preserve recovery for reasonably foreseeable chain damages.

Subject: Re: MSA redlines — damages carve-outs (analysis + proposed language)

Evelyn / team — quick memo below to frame negotiation posture and proposed text options. I’ll be on the call Tue if scheduled.

Summary of risk trade-offs:
- Foreseeability: broader; allows recovery where loss was a foreseeable outcome of the breach even if not directly caused. Easier for counterparty to argue chain damages.
- Proximate causation: narrower standard if drafted to require direct causal nexus; reduces Redwood's exposure to remote downstream losses. But proximate cause language can be litigated and relies on jurisdictional interpretation.
- One-way carveouts: operationally exposes Redwood to asymmetric liability. If Acme insists, we should limit to specific, enumerated categories (e.g., court-ordered fines for data breach, notification costs, forensic costs) and keep a strict per-claim/aggregate cap tethered to Order Form fees.

Recommended negotiation posture:
1) Prefer mutual exclusion of consequential/special/incidental/punitive damages with a proximate-cause tie-breaker defined narrowly. This balances clarity and reciprocity.
2) If Acme insists on a one-way data-breach carveout, accept only for narrow, enumerated remediation costs and only where damages are direct and documented, subject to a separate sub-cap equal to 12 months of Order Form fees; statute-driven fines/penalties remain excluded unless mandated by law.

Proposed clause options (pick one in negotiations):

Option A (mutual, proximate-cause):
"Neither party shall be liable to the other for any consequential, special, incidental, indirect, exemplary or punitive damages ("Excluded Damages"); provided, however, that Excluded Damages shall not include direct damages proximately caused by a Party's gross negligence or willful misconduct. For purposes of this Section, "proximately caused" means damages that are the natural and proximate result of the party's breach and do not include damages attributable solely to the intervening acts of third parties or remote consequential losses."

Option B (mutual + foreseeability fallback):
"...Excluded Damages shall not include direct damages that were reasonably foreseeable to the parties at the time of contracting and proximately caused by the breaching party's act or omission..."

Option C (one-way, narrow data-breach carveout):
"Notwithstanding the foregoing, Customer may recover from Supplier, subject to the Order Form sub-cap below, direct remediation costs (reasonable notification costs, credit monitoring fees, and forensic investigation costs) that are demonstrably and directly caused by Supplier's willful misconduct or gross negligence in connection with the processing of Customer data. Such recovery shall be capped at an amount equal to twelve (12) months of fees paid under the applicable Order Form and shall not include consequential or lost-profit claims."

Practical negotiation notes:
- Keep the term "proximate" but define it (avoid importing common law variability).
- Tie any one-way carveout to objective categories and a clear sub-cap. Avoid blanket language that opens the door to remote economic losses.
- Reserve right to carve-in statutory indemnities (e.g., data protection fines) only where required by law; otherwise exclude.

I attached a clean redline with Option A as our baseline and Option C flagged as alternative if Acme won't accept reciprocity.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Laura — +1 on Option A as baseline. Two quick operational points from risk:

1) If we accept a sub-cap for the data-breach carveout, we should ensure it's an aggregate cap per customer-year, not per incident; otherwise frequency risk is uncontrolled.
2) Add an explicit exclusion for punitive and exemplary damages under all circumstances — call this out separately so there is no ambiguity.

I attached a suggested redline (redline_MSA_risk_20260303.docx) with small tweaks to the cap language and an explicit punitive-exclusion clause.

Samantha / Tom — thanks for the thoughtful redline. We looked into this internally and want to propose a compromise to take into the call:

Inline proposed compromise (cleaned):
"Neither party will be liable to the other for consequential, special, incidental, indirect, punitive or exemplary damages ("Excluded Damages"); provided, however, that Excluded Damages shall not include direct damages proximately caused by the breaching party's gross negligence or willful misconduct. 

For clarity, for purposes of this Agreement, "proximately caused" means damages that were the natural and proximate result of the party's breach and that are not attributable solely to intervening third-party conduct or remote downstream losses.

Notwithstanding the foregoing, Customer may recover direct, documented remediation costs resulting from Supplier's gross negligence or willful misconduct in connection with the processing of Customer data limited to reasonable notification, forensic investigation and credit monitoring fees, subject to an aggregate sub-cap equal to twelve (12) months of fees paid under the applicable Order Form (per customer, per twelve (12) month period). Statutory fines and penalties shall only be recoverable to the extent required by applicable law."

We believe this preserves reciprocity while giving Acme a narrowly tailored, one-way recovery path for immediate remediation costs (if your GC still needs that). It also adds an explicit punitive/exemplary exclusion and an aggregate annual sub-cap per Markus' suggestion.

If that reads OK, let's take it on the call. Can you confirm Tue 8:30 AM PT (Mar 9) or Wed 9:00 AM PT? If neither works, propose alternatives and we’ll adjust.

Thanks,
